info.name: OpenSetlist API
info.description:
Manual walkthrough for session auth (#7) and role enforcement (#14).

Before starting: `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d db && pnpm -C api db:migrate` gives you a fresh database (the existing dev data is all test junk).

Postman automatically stores and sends cookies per domain, so Register/Login keep you logged in across requests. To test the guest-vs-manager flow, log out (or switch user via Login) between the two roles.

Expected flow on a fresh database:
1. Register -> first user becomes group_manager of the lazily created single group
2. Register again (second user) -> joins as member
3. List members -> see both roles
4. As the second user: PATCH/DELETE -> 403
5. As the first user: PATCH role, DELETE member -> 200
6. Demote the only manager -> 409 (last-manager lockout guard)
7. Songs folder: Create song -> songId saved as a collection variable
8. Arrangements folder: List/Create under {{songId}} (Create saves arrangementId), then Get/Update/Delete by id — Update with a stale version demonstrates the 409

Maintenance rule (AGENTS.md): every new endpoint lands together with its entry here, including example responses.

request.description: Creates the user, the single group (if it does not exist yet), and the membership — one transaction. First-ever member: group_manager, later ones: member. Auto-login: response sets the session cookie. Duplicate email: 409. Short password: 400.

response.name: 400 Invalid input

request.description: Sets a fresh 30-day session cookie. Wrong password and unknown email return the same 401 message — the API never confirms which emails exist. Tip: change the email variable and login to switch user (the cookie jar follows the last login).
Who am I, based on the session cookie. 200 with the user, or 401 when not logged in / session expired.
Revokes the session row and clears the cookie. POST (not GET) so a stray link cannot log you out. 200 always.

exec: console.log('memberId set to first member: ' + body.members[0].email + ' (' + body.members[0].role + ')');

request.description: Visible to every group member — readers included (authorize('reader')). Anonymous: 401. The test script stores the FIRST member's id into {{memberId}} — on a fresh database that is the first manager, i.e. you.

Requires group_manager (or superadmin). Body role: reader | member | group_manager. Reader/member attempting: 403. Invalid role: 400. Unknown member id: 404. Demoting the LAST group_manager: 409 — the lockout guard. Try it with the body role 'member' against yourself on a fresh database.

response.name: 409 Last manager lockout

request.description: Requires group_manager (or superadmin). Removing the LAST group_manager: 409. Note: even a superadmin hits that 409 — the guard lives in the service layer, below the role ladder, on purpose.

response.name: 409 Last manager lockout

request.description: All songs of the group, newest first. Any role incl. reader; 401 when anonymous.

reader+. Body carries a filter tree — leaves { search?, tagsAll?, tagsAny? } combine with { and: [...] } / { or: [...] }, nestable. tagsAll = song has EVERY listed tag (AND), tagsAny = at least one (OR); names are normalized (trim + lowercase). No filter = whole library.

response.name: 400 Invalid input (empty filter leaf)

request.description: member+ only (403 for readers). defaultKey must be one of C C# D Eb E F F# G Ab A Bb B; language is an optional 2-letter ISO 639-1 code.

response.name: 400 Invalid input

request.description: member+ only. Tolerant seed format (see api/fixtures/dev-seed.json): unknown keys are stripped. Arrangements are imported too — snake_case keys map to the API shape and go through the same validation (unique section labels, default_sequence ⊆ labels), so a bad arrangement fails the whole import with 400. Tags are stored too (normalized, created inline). The song's defaultKey falls back to the first arrangement's original_key, else C. One transaction: a mid-file failure rolls back everything.

response.name: 400 Invalid input (e.g. sequence references an unknown section label)

request.description: Any role incl. reader. 404 when the id is unknown or belongs to another group.
member+ only. All fields optional, but version is required — send the version you last saw. The server check-and-bumps; a stale version gets 409 (optimistic locking).

response.name: 409 Conflict (stale version)

request.description: member+ only, version-checked like PATCH. Arrangements of the song cascade-delete.

response.name: 409 Conflict (stale version)

request.description: reader+. 404 when the song doesn't exist in the group.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: member+ only (403 for readers). Sections hold the ABC notation; defaultSequence entries must be existing section labels (repeats allowed), labels must be unique — otherwise 400. 404 when the song doesn't exist.

response.name: 201 Created
400 Invalid input (unknown sequence label)

request.description: reader+.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: member+ only. Full-body PATCH — the section editor always sends the whole arrangement. version must be the one you last saw; a stale version gets 409 (optimistic locking), unknown id 404.

response.name: 200 OK
400 Invalid input (duplicate labels)
409 Conflict (stale version)

request.description: member+ only, version-checked like PATCH (send the version you last saw; here 1 right after Create). Setlist items referencing it cascade-delete.

response.name: 409 Conflict (stale version)

request.description: reader+. The group's tag vocabulary (group-scoped, lowercase-normalized), alphabetical — autocomplete source for the song form.

group_manager only (403 for members/readers; platform superadmin bypasses). Removes the tag from every song — song_tags cascades. Create a tag by saving a song that carries it; there is no standalone create endpoint.
